agent: W2-8 defender: K > 1 belongs in PAR 4
summary: I accept CL-1 in a stronger form: on the heavy files the hub cell takes 96–98.5 % of fire time, but the limit is the dependency chain, not the home rule. The BSP-trace DAG's critical path equals the per-round span to within 2–3 %, so under every placement (cell, component, propagator, ideal LPT), and even running asynchronously, K > 1 is bounded at 1.22–1.28× (constraints-adversarial) and 1.45–1.55× (type-adversarial). Real executors injected with no rebuild measure 0.84–0.96× on S0 there and 0.49–0.74× on the small files, so the verdict on the charge question is 'fails' for every workload that propagates; only the repo's PAR 2 micro networks reach ≥ 1.5× (1.55–1.90×), and they do no propagation (one round, 0 productive fires). I concede the expensive half of D.2 §6.7 to C10-6's sequel (owned slots, lanes, the detector and the fence): asynchrony buys ≤ 3 % on today's workloads, and CL-3, CL-4 and CL-12 are its costs. I defend keeping in PAR 4 a round-synchronous K > 1 frontier step (BSP-K) whose fires run against one snapshot, are placed dynamically and are folded in pid order, so the schedule does not depend on K and it needs no detector, no fence and no ownership. It was measured result-identical at K = 4 and 8 with a mutant power row, it gives 1.83–2.78× on S0 for wide productive frontiers, and DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.org:846-848 already places per-network parallelism there. It must be decided in P2, which rewrites the S0 loop, and it ships with a per-run K defaulting to 1 (conceding C6-5). Its first elaboration workload needs P2-lite plus batching of independent commands, an ESTIMATE whose bound is ≈ K.

verdicts.evidence:
THEOREM. Hypotheses:
- each fire is a function of the snapshot alone: no shared mutable state, and every ambient read gives the same value on every thread;
- the fold order is the pid order of the worklist;
- whether a frontier step is taken, and what it contains, is a function of the network state alone, independent of K and of timing.

defence.position: P3 stays in PAR 4, but in a changed form. K > 1 is a round-synchronous frontier step (BSP-K) whose schedule is a function of the network alone, behind a per-run K whose default is 1. D.2 §6.7's asynchronous design moves to the sequel C10-6 proposes: owned slots, lanes, the Mattern detector, the fence, and per-cell or per-component homes.
concessions: CL-1 holds, and is worse than stated. By time the hub's fires carry 96–98.5 % of fire time, and the per-cell busiest share by time is 0.96–0.99.

Component ownership (CL-1's direction) does not rescue elaboration at K > 1. Time-weighted parallelism stays at 1.19–1.35, and ideal LPT gives 1.24–1.46. The binding limit is the dependency chain (DAG CP ≈ round span), not balance.

No language-level workload in the corpus gives ≥ 1.5× on S0 at K > 1 under any ownership unit. Realized: 0.84–0.96× on the heavy files and 0.49–0.74× on the small ones. Bounds: ≤ 1.28× and ≤ 1.55× on the heavy files, even asynchronously and with the in-fire whole-map protocol removed.

The files whose S0 is not hub-concentrated (atms-adversarial, solve-adversarial) have 0.07–0.15 ms of S0, under 1 % of their run. scheduler-adversarial is hub-concentrated (0.87 / 0.95). parity-adversarial crashes (DEFERRED 153). There is nothing there to parallelize.
The repo's existing K > 1 evidence measures parallel ceremony on fires that do nothing: PAR 2's demos and P0 §10.1's 1.20× / 1.51×. The narrowing networks that do pay are my constructions.
Asynchrony buys ≤ 3 % over rounds on today's workloads. So D.2 §6.7's detector, lanes, owned slots and fence have no measured return in PAR 4, and C10-6 holds for that half.
CL-4 (a)–(g) hold as defects of D.2's fence. I answer them by removing the fence from P3, not by repairing it.
C6-5 holds. K is a machine budget: it defaults to 1, the runner uses 1, and the executors cost 4–16 % of S0 when they cannot help.
The production executor is a live defect: 0.44–0.52× S0 on the heavy files and 0.10–0.20× on the small ones (CL-2, replicated with the threshold off). P0.5 should delete it.

No near-term workload sits inside PAR 4's horizon. User-level networks (net-run → capture-network → run-to-quiescence, reduction.rkt:4451-4456, prop-observatory.rkt:164-171) are used by 0 .prologos files in the repo. BSP-LE 3 is a seed (docs/tracking/2026-07-20_BSP_LE_TRACK3_ONNET_SEED.md), and the on-network solver gives wrong answers today (PD-1).
Today the merge phase is 52–53 % of heavy-file S0, so BSP-K's Amdahl ceiling with a serial merge is ≤ 1.9× even with infinitely parallel fires. P2-lite's keyed merges and diffs (W2-2) come first.
defence.argument: (1) A K > 1 design exists that is correct without CL-3, CL-4 or CL-12, and it is the one the principles already name. DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.org:846-848 puts per-network parallelism at "work distribution within one BSP round, or Gauss-Seidel sub-round", and :798-800 keeps the scheduler's smarts to efficiency. In a frontier step, every queued fire reads the same snapshot, so dynamic placement is free and no ownership unit exists. Results are folded in pid order by the cells' own merges, so K cannot change the result, even for the non-join cells D.2 wanted to fence; there is nothing to fence. The empty worklist on the orchestrator is quiescence, so no detector is needed. Measured: identical results and per-round fingerprints at K = 4 and 8, against a mutant power row. (2) It pays where the workload is wide: 1.83–2.78× on S0 for productive frontiers of 6 000–30 000 fires, using real fire-and-collect-writes and bulk-merge-writes and nothing but an injected executor. The crossover is about 0.3–0.7 ms of fire work per step. Asynchrony would add ≤ 3 % on today's traces, so the cheap design captures essentially all the K > 1 value that today's DAGs contain. (3) The decision belongs to this track because P2 rewrites the S0 inner loop now. If P2's DIRECT loop keeps a frontier Jacobi step, K > 1 later is an executor lambda plus a pool (about 60 lines in w28-bspk.rkt). The step's body is BSP's inner loop, which D.2 keeps anyway as the replay oracle (§6.6; R-6). If P2 drops round structure, the only K > 1 route left is §6.7's machinery, and CL-3, CL-4 and CL-12 reopen in the sequel. (4) Elaboration's parallelism lies between commands, not within one. The heavy files run 66 and 61 S0 runs in sequence, one per top-level command. The longest has CP 1.11 ms of the file's 16.6 ms, and 0.39 of 7.8 ms. If independent commands shared one S0 run (PPN 4C's module network, or concurrent runs), the DAG bound is ≈ K: 4.0, 8.0 and 15–16 (ESTIMATE; the hypothesis is that the commands are independent, which inferred types that later commands read violate). Such batches produce exactly the wide frontiers that BSP-K exploits, provided P2-lite has removed the serial whole-map merge. (5) Determinism by construction is a correctness asset, not only a speed knob. The P3 parity suite reduces to equality at K ∈ {1, 4, 8, 16}, with no S-9 alternation semantics and no replay-at-K > 1 triage.
defence.design_that_would_make_it_pay:
Information flow.
(a) Cells. S0 cells are unchanged: the CHAMP stays primary (γ1), and there are no owned slots. Each S0 run's network carries one per-run input cell, s0-k (CL-11's per-run K), with default 1; the caller sets it (runner 1; LSP and CLI ≤ cores − 2; never oversubscribed, C6-5). A per-run frontier threshold W, in fires or estimated fire-µs, is scheduler data taken from a committed crossover table. It does not depend on K, so K never changes the schedule.
(b) Scheduler. P2's DIRECT loop reads its worklist. When the frontier is at least W, it takes one Jacobi step:
- every queued propagator fires against the same snapshot pointer;
- each fire's write deltas are folded into the network in pid order by the cells' merges;
- with K > 1 the fires are computed by K executors, each taking the next index from a CAS counter.
Otherwise the loop runs DIRECT as at K = 1. Quiescence is the orchestrator's empty worklist, and a contradiction is checked once per step.
(c) Executors. Either a make-parallel-thread-pool created once per process, with fresh Racket threads per step that inherit the parameterization exactly as today's executor does, or parked persistent workers that install a parameterization captured per step (CL-13's interim). No spinning, because of GC stop-the-world time (C6-5).
(d) Gates.
- Equality of results and per-step fingerprints at K ∈ {1, 4, 8, 16}, with a drop-one-result power row (w28-bspk.rkt's shape).
- ≥ 1.5× on S0 at K = 8 on a named wide workload class. Today that is the intersection-merge networks, which should replace bench-parallel-demos' union demos; later, user networks and BSP-LE 3.
- No change at K = 1.
(e) Order of value. P0.5 deletes the production executor. P2-lite's keyed diff and delta merges take the 52 % serial merge out of BSP-K's way. Batching commands (PPN 4C) gives elaboration wide frontiers.
(f) The sequel (C10-6) builds asynchronous DIRECT-K only if some workload shows a DAG critical path well below its round span, which none in the repo does. It would use component-keyed deltas from P2-lite as the lane payload.
